### Considered and refused

- 1473 ‘bearn’ i “son” against l “child”: matches the five earlier occurrences exactly.
- 1474 l “you famous kinsman” for vocative ‘se mǣra maga’: ‘maga’ is “son/kinsman”; the word order is transparent; kept.
- 1484 ‘brēac’ taking an object “him”: grammar (brūcan with genitive/instrumental) makes it doubtful, but the note already calls it a guess; refused as a change.
- 1484 ‘þonne mōste’ “while I might”: acceptable force; kept.
- 1492 “Weder-Geats’” in l with Weder unexplained: note says it is guessed; published parts use “Weders”; kept as is.
- 1497 “hundred seasons” in i: published Fitt II i uses “season” for ‘missēra’; kept.
- 1497 masculine ‘sē’: note correct; Fitt XXI explains 1392 by ‘māga’, so “the same oddity” is loose but harmless; refused.
- 1506 ‘hringa þengel’ as “kenning for Beowulf as giver and owner of rings”: speculative, but it is the plain reading of the title; refused.
- 1518 ‘grundwyrgenne’ “accusative feminine”: correct; guess already flagged.
- 1529 ‘læt’ adjective vs imperative ‘lǣt’ at 1488: forms checked, labels true.
- 1534 ‘dôn’ circumflex called a contraction mark: matches the convention; refused.
- 1537 “be eaxle”/‘feaxe’: note correct to the apparatus.
- 1543 ‘oferwearp’ crux: note and i follow the cruces file; l has no object, as the text; refused any change.
- 1550 ‘forsīðod’: lexicon reading, flagged moderately sure in cruces only; left unmarked in the note, low risk.
- 1553 “ruled the victory” (i) versus ‘gescēd’ “decided”: ‘geweldan’ is “control”; kept.
- First dot under a vowel (‘getrūwọde’, 1533) is explained once, as required; no earlier dot in this part.
- No remembered-English problems beyond those fixed; “stiff and steel-edged”, “the strongest of warriors”, “Ruler of the heavens” were rebuilt-from-grammar and checked.

- 1543 ‘oferwearp’: crux, already flagged; no change.
- 1550 ‘forsīðod’: note unflagged though cruces file says “moderately sure”; Pass 1 refusal stands.
- Whether ‘heorogīfre’ is “fierce” or “sword”: flagged as guess in note and now in the gloss.

### Considered and refused (gloss)

- ‘dryhten’ (human lord, 1484): shared entry says “lord”, adding only that it can be God; covers.
- ‘feorhgenīðlan’ “in apposition to hine” (shared example): the form and sense are covered; the example is the old context; broadening would only restate it.
- ‘þē’ (1482) relative: first shared reading covers it; its remark about emendation does not apply here but entries are never rewritten.
- ‘gemyndig’, ‘heard’, ‘gist’, ‘sunu’, ‘þæs’ (1509 adverbial), ‘wið’, ‘ymb’, ‘forma’, ‘sīð’: shared readings checked against each line and cover the use.
- ‘hearde’ new adjective reading (1553): kept; hedged in the entry itself, and the unit’s `l` takes it as the adjective.
